trigger: Multi-day loss or destructive misuse of a common enterprise platform (identity or endpoint management, ERP or MES SaaS, supplier portal or EDI service) used by many manufacturers and suppliers
propagation_mechanism: Simultaneous loss of ordering, scheduling, shipping and invoicing across many firms; plants stop on precaution while OT may be untouched
affected_sector_service: Order-to-cash, production scheduling, logistics release, supplier payments
plausible_effects: Correlated output and delivery gaps across counterparties; concurrent working-capital draws; deferred revenue; disputes over force majeure
early_warning_indicators: Provider outage or breach notices; government alerts on platform misuse; leak-site claims against platform users; KEV additions for ERP or file-transfer products
assumptions: Platform unavailable for three to ten days; no OT compromise; durations illustrative; no probability assigned
limitations: No in-period multi-day common-platform failure across many manufacturers was found; offline fallback and multi-tenant isolation limit breadth

trigger: Ransomware or destructive intrusion at a high-volume OEM or tier-1 supplier triggers a precautionary global shutdown of IT and production
propagation_mechanism: Just-in-time call-offs stop; tier-1 to tier-3 suppliers idle; dealers and logistics lose volume; restart is phased by plant
affected_sector_service: Vehicle, device or consumer-goods production and delivery; supplier receivables
plausible_effects: Weeks of lost output; GBP hundreds of millions of cash outflow at the OEM; supplier liquidity stress; government or customer-funded support; national output effect
early_warning_indicators: Company incident notices and 8-K or exchange filings; production-pause extensions; supplier lay-off announcements; requests for state support
assumptions: Four- to eight-week stop at one large manufacturer (informed by JLR); no probability assigned
limitations: Segmented firms restored within weeks (Stryker); buffered inventory and multi-sourcing reduce cascade

trigger: Compromise or exploitation of a shared supplier layer: an OT vendor's fielded controllers, a system integrator or managed IT provider, or a widely used component supplier
propagation_mechanism: One supplier's weakness reaches many customers at once (fleet of exposed controllers; provider access into several plants; packaging or component shortage)
affected_sector_service: Field equipment performance and safety; customer production lines; product recalls and liability
plausible_effects: Correlated customer losses; product-liability and warranty claims; regulator reporting; replacement of end-of-life equipment
early_warning_indicators: National CERT alerts naming products; exchange disclosures citing an IT provider; leak-site claims against integrators; end-of-support notices
assumptions: Exposure persists in end-of-life fleets; customer segmentation incomplete; no probability assigned
limitations: French case propagated through internet exposure of many units rather than a vendor breach; vendor patches exist for current firmware
